inspiration.attribution: Thibaud Colas's audit-type taxonomy informs these project classifications; every decision applies to the current criterion wording.

classificationMeaning: The primary class identifies the evidence and judgment needed for the complete current criterion within a declared audit scope. Supporting classes identify useful partial methods. Classes describe assessment potential, not implemented checks, audit results or W3C-endorsed conformance.

classDefinitions.static analysis: Structural analysis of code, declarations or configuration can decide the scoped criterion without exercising an interactive journey. The required source may be public or provided separately.
classDefinitions.automated: A repeatable runtime or HTTP procedure can decide the scoped criterion from explicit observable states or outputs. Applicability and representative scope still need to be set.
classDefinitions.manual, quantitative: A reviewer defines a task, experiment, comparison or threshold, then interprets repeatable measurements. Agents and deterministic tools can perform much of this work.
classDefinitions.manual, qualitative: Judging meaning, relevance, usability, architecture or adequacy requires contextual interpretation of behavior or materials. These may be public or supplied source and records. LLM review remains evidence-bound and needs evaluation.
classDefinitions.consulting: Judging the criterion requires organizational decisions, governance, resourcing, specialist context or evidence of sustained practice. Sufficient records may be public or supplied by the owner. Private source or traces alone do not make a criterion consulting; technical analysis can remain quantitative, qualitative or automated.

evidenceAccessDefinitions.public-site: Live pages, responses, delivered assets and interactions, including an authorized test account where required.
evidenceAccessDefinitions.public-documents: Published policies, disclosures, reports, documentation and attributable public records.
evidenceAccessDefinitions.source: Relevant implementation, configuration, manifests and history, public or explicitly provided.
evidenceAccessDefinitions.owner-records: Project-specific records, measurements or operational evidence provided by the responsible organization; equivalent published records can satisfy the same need.

criteria.title: Impact analysis
criteria.rationale: Periodic impact assessment and demonstrated progress require organizational evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review dated assessments, material issues, public reporting and actions across at least two review periods.

criteria.title: External impact
criteria.rationale: Supply-chain and non-digital impacts cannot be established from browser behavior.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect the impact boundary, logistics and infrastructure evidence, reduction plan and measured follow-through.

criteria.title: Audience evaluation
criteria.rationale: Identifying affected groups and involving them requires research records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review recruitment, participant coverage, findings and decisions; compare them with the service's public tasks.

criteria.title: Sustainable brand development
criteria.rationale: Asset measurements do not establish approved branding requirements or recurring review.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare brand requirements, asset variants and review records; measure representative published assets.

criteria.title: Wireframes and prototypes
criteria.rationale: A finished interface does not reveal whether early prototypes informed development.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect prototypes, tests and decisions showing which risks or unnecessary work were avoided.

criteria.title: Participation and testing
criteria.rationale: Participation throughout design requires evidence of who influenced decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review participant selection, session records, feedback and resulting design changes.

criteria.title: Environmental ideation
criteria.rationale: Environmental boundaries and non-human needs must be evidenced in ideation decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect impact assumptions, personas or equivalent methods, and decisions traceable to them.

criteria.title: Efficient paths
criteria.rationale: Task efficiency can be compared through a defined journey and measurable steps, with usability judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Define representative tasks; record actions, elapsed time, choices and completion, then review unnecessary friction.

criteria.title: Patterns for efficiency
criteria.rationale: Recognizable patterns and clear journeys depend on task and audience interpretation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Complete representative tasks and compare interaction patterns, consistency and explanations with familiar conventions.

criteria.title: Content discovery
criteria.rationale: Finding useful content and evaluating navigation clarity requires contextual judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Test representative information-finding tasks through navigation, search, sitemap and update channels; inspect freshness.

criteria.title: Respect user attention
criteria.rationale: Meaningful control of attention is broader than detecting notification buttons.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise information-delivery controls and defaults during tasks; assess interruption, choice and cognitive demands.

criteria.title: Distraction-free design
criteria.rationale: Deciding what is relevant or safely removable requires user-task and accessibility judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Observe initial and interactive states; assess interruptions, optional assets and essential information before suggesting removal.

criteria.title: Remove engagement traps
criteria.rationale: Intent and unnecessary engagement cannot be inferred from scroll mechanics alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise feeds, pagination and browser controls; assess whether continuation or navigation restrictions serve the task.

criteria.title: Deceptive design patterns
criteria.rationale: Pressure, misleading claims and choice asymmetry require interpretation of the complete flow.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare alternatives, defaults, disclosures and consequences through consent, registration, purchasing and cancellation tasks.

criteria.title: Advertisements
criteria.rationale: Disclosure clarity, disruption and meaningful user control require qualitative review alongside measurements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect advertisement labels and controls, exercise dismissal and measure loading cost in representative states.

criteria.title: Analytics and tracking
criteria.rationale: Consent behavior is observable, but deciding whether tracking is necessary needs purpose evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace requests before and after consent, compare declared purposes, and request justification for unexplained tracking.

criteria.title: Search Engine Optimization
criteria.rationale: User-serving content and manipulation cannot be decided from metadata presence alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review representative content, duplicate pages and accessibility-related metadata for usefulness and misleading optimization.

criteria.title: Deliverables reusability
criteria.rationale: Reusable formats and practical reuse need examination of the delivered material.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect representative deliverables for open formats, exportability, licensing and usable structure.

criteria.title: Deliverables documentation
criteria.rationale: Maintained documentation and replacement processes require evidence across releases.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect technical guidance, ownership, change history and examples of retiring or replacing obsolete information.

criteria.title: Deliverables readability
criteria.rationale: Access and understandable source documentation can be reviewed, but quality is interpretive.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect source access, comments and contributor guidance against a representative maintenance or reuse task.

criteria.title: Design system
criteria.rationale: Visual consistency does not establish component governance, ownership and maintenance.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect component reuse and page payloads alongside system ownership, versions, standards and documentation history.

criteria.title: Need for media
criteria.rationale: Whether media aids understanding is a content and user-task judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review each sampled media item's purpose and an alternative without it; preserve meaningful and accessible content.

criteria.title: Optimized media
criteria.rationale: Format, size and rendering comparisons are measurable but need acceptable-quality and device constraints.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare delivered dimensions, compression, formats and native playback across representative devices and user needs.

criteria.title: Lazy loading
criteria.rationale: Choosing critical media and demonstrating deferred transfer needs a scoped interaction experiment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Record above-fold requests, then interaction and scroll requests; verify critical media remains available without premature heavy downloads.

criteria.title: User-controlled media
criteria.rationale: Playback, resolution and low-data choices need a repeatable interaction checklist with understandable labels.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise initial playback, controls and lower-bandwidth alternatives; verify length, format and data-use disclosures against assets.

criteria.title: Media management and use
criteria.rationale: A media lifecycle policy and its application require project records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review compression, performance, retention and deletion requirements plus examples of their use.

criteria.title: Need for animation
criteria.rationale: Animation's contribution to understanding or task completion is interpretive.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare animated and reduced-motion states for meaning, task support and unnecessary distraction.

criteria.title: Avoiding overburdening
criteria.rationale: Animation load and replay frequency can be measured against a scoped performance and attention assessment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Count concurrent animations and replays, profile rendering, and test constrained devices and motion preferences.

criteria.title: Control animation
criteria.rationale: Start, pause, stop and other controls can be exercised through explicit state assertions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trigger representative animations and verify the required controls actually change or stop their state.

criteria.title: Efficient animation
criteria.rationale: Comparing rendering cost needs controlled measurements and acceptable-output constraints.
criteria.reviewRoute: Profile equivalent native and custom animation variants for main-thread work, layout, frame delivery and visual function.

criteria.title: Pre-installed typefaces
criteria.rationale: Font declarations and referenced assets identify reliance on pre-installed fonts.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect font-family and font-face declarations; confirm a cold visit does not fetch avoidable custom fonts.

criteria.title: Web font optimization
criteria.rationale: Required axes, font complexity, fallbacks and loading behavior need measured comparison.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory font files and ranges, compare alternatives, and test fallback readability during delayed and failed loading.

criteria.title: Web font subsetting
criteria.rationale: Safe subsetting depends on declared language coverage and dynamic-input requirements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare font coverage with supported scripts and content; test missing glyphs, dynamic input and incremental delivery where applicable.

criteria.title: Need for notification
criteria.rationale: Notification necessity and preference alignment cannot be judged from permission state alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect opt-in flows and delivered messages against their stated purpose; use delivery records where the public flow is insufficient.

criteria.title: Notification settings
criteria.rationale: Visible, accessible and easy controls need task-based interpretation as well as state checks.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise notification defaults, settings, unsubscribe, logout and account closure with a representative account.

criteria.title: Printed documents
criteria.rationale: Print layouts and page counts are measurable, while unnecessary paper depends on workflow context.
criteria.reviewRoute: Print representative real content, compare page counts and usability, and review digital alternatives through the same task.

criteria.title: Optimized documents
criteria.rationale: Document size and format comparisons need accessibility and suitability checks.
criteria.reviewRoute: Measure downloadable files, compare compressed or HTML alternatives and verify reading and assistive-technology access.

criteria.title: Optimized delivery
criteria.rationale: Reuse and generation behavior require controlled requests plus server traces; private evidence does not change the quantitative method.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect generation and cache configuration with processing traces; test reuse and cookie-free delivery where relevant.

criteria.title: Labels and choice
criteria.rationale: Pre-download summaries and suitable language/format choices require content interpretation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect document links before activation and verify names, formats, sizes, summaries and available alternatives.

criteria.title: Early user testing
criteria.rationale: Representative-user validation requires research and prototyping records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review testing processes, participants, real-world conditions, findings and resulting feature changes.

criteria.title: Ongoing evaluation
criteria.rationale: One audit cannot establish an ongoing multidisciplinary evaluation program.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect dated UX, code, performance, accessibility and security reviews with issue resolution records.

criteria.title: Automated tests
criteria.rationale: A test file does not establish critical coverage or consistent execution across releases.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect suite scope, CI configuration and recent run histories; trace representative regressions to tests.

criteria.title: Performance testing
criteria.rationale: Per-release monitoring and corrective action require longitudinal project evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review laboratory and real-user measurements across releases, bottleneck investigations and verified fixes.

criteria.title: Usage changes
criteria.rationale: Feature feedback, adoption and churn are normally project-specific usage evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review scoped analytics and feedback with decisions showing how they informed releases.

criteria.title: Usability testing
criteria.rationale: Repeated user research and measured follow-through require participant and delivery evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace usability findings and real-user metrics to changes, then inspect post-release validation.

criteria.title: Compatibility documentation
criteria.rationale: Public support lists can be read, but regular review requires versioned maintenance evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review supported platforms and versions alongside dated updates and the process for keeping them current.

criteria.title: Maintaining compatibility
criteria.rationale: Avoiding planned obsolescence requires support decisions and security/operational tradeoffs over time.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare supported releases, compatibility tests, security constraints and user-facing update explanations.

criteria.title: User constraints
criteria.rationale: A declared browser, device and network matrix makes compatibility checks repeatable.
criteria.reviewRoute: Run key tasks across representative constrained connections, browsers and older devices; record failures and limits of emulation.

criteria.title: Performance goals
criteria.rationale: Choosing project-specific limits requires declared goals and ownership rather than observed page size alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect resource and performance targets, rationale, owners and the thresholds used to judge delivery.

criteria.title: Energy intensity
criteria.rationale: Lower-impact choices require matched resource measurements and a user-value comparison.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare equivalent components under controlled conditions; retain energy-model limits and the value of intensive features.

criteria.title: Minified code
criteria.rationale: Delivered code and data can be checked for minification and functional regressions within the sample.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect response bodies for avoidable minification overhead and rerun representative functionality after transformation.

criteria.title: Remove redundancy
criteria.rationale: Non-execution in one visit is not proof that code is unused; coverage needs a scoped task matrix.
criteria.reviewRoute: Collect coverage across initial and interactive states, inspect build/source reachability and verify candidate removal with regressions.

criteria.title: Code splitting
criteria.rationale: Loading boundaries and splitting overhead require comparison across task and cache states.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace module downloads during tasks, compare cold and repeat visits, and assess excessive requests or duplicated chunks.

criteria.title: Remove or simplify
criteria.rationale: Safe structural simplification requires qualitative source review, supported by duplication and performance measurements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect duplicated logic, shared abstractions, tests and before/after performance and maintainability evidence.

criteria.title: Iteration over recreation
criteria.rationale: Whether rebuilding is justified depends on decision history, effort and projected benefits.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare reuse and replacement options using user value, performance, scalability and maintenance evidence.

criteria.title: Organize code arrangement
criteria.rationale: The balance between reuse, complexity and maintainability requires source-level interpretation rather than duplicate counts alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect representative CSS/JavaScript refactors, dependencies, tests and performance rather than duplicate counts alone.

criteria.title: Assess and reduce
criteria.rationale: Supplier standards, dependency risks and early assessments require procurement and governance evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory third parties, measure delivery costs, and review necessity, contractual standards and exit or portability options.

criteria.title: Third-party implementation
criteria.rationale: Interaction-gated third-party requests and available alternatives can be asserted in a browser.
criteria.reviewRoute: Record requests before interaction and after activation; verify a direct or lightweight alternative where offered.

criteria.title: Self-hosting
criteria.rationale: Practical self-hosting requires interpreting infrastructure control, requirements and feasible delivery alternatives.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory asset origins and review ownership, hosting constraints, reliability and relevant self-hosting alternatives.

criteria.title: Third-party preferences
criteria.rationale: Working opt-out controls require a defined before/after interaction and request comparison.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise each non-essential third-party control and verify its effect on requests and functionality.

criteria.title: Semantic code
criteria.rationale: Markup validity and standard conformance have deterministic structural checks.
criteria.reviewRoute: Validate representative delivered and generated markup; distinguish syntax failures from broader accessibility judgments.

criteria.title: Optional features
criteria.rationale: Omitting syntax safely depends on readability, accessibility and rendering tradeoffs.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare candidate omissions with validator, browser and accessibility results; retain syntax that improves clarity or compatibility.

criteria.title: Non-standard code
criteria.rationale: Exceptions for compatibility or accessibility need justification beyond deprecation detection.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory obsolete or proprietary features and polyfills, then assess supported-browser needs and removal evidence.

criteria.title: Custom code
criteria.rationale: Whether a native feature meets the requirement needs functional and maintainability judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare custom components with platform alternatives for required behavior, accessibility, reuse and resource use.

criteria.title: Asynchronous code
criteria.rationale: Criticality and render effects require timed observations, not only async/defer attributes.
criteria.reviewRoute: Record the loading waterfall and visual states under constrained networks; verify deferred assets do not break essential rendering.

criteria.title: Optimized loading
criteria.rationale: The value of priority hints depends on measured competition and loading order.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare equivalent loads with and without hints; inspect request priorities, critical rendering and wasted preload transfer.

criteria.title: Required elements
criteria.rationale: Title presence is static, but useful optional head elements require context.
criteria.reviewRoute: Validate head structure and review whether titles and optional elements improve the sampled task without unnecessary work.

criteria.title: Meta tags
criteria.rationale: Metadata must be relevant and meaningful, not merely present or syntactically valid.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect browser and sharing metadata against page content and intended use; flag missing, misleading or redundant values.

criteria.title: Structured data
criteria.rationale: Schema validity is automatable, while faithful interpretation and reusable meaning need review.
criteria.reviewRoute: Parse structured data, compare entities and properties with visible content, and test intended consumer use.

criteria.title: Media and preference queries
criteria.rationale: Preference support needs a repeatable state matrix and a judgment of where each preference benefits users.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise supported color, contrast, motion, data, transparency, print and scripting states; compare behavior and resource use.

criteria.title: Device-adaptable
criteria.rationale: Cross-device behavior requires representative viewport, capability and task measurements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Run essential tasks across device sizes and missing-feature states, recording overflow, blocked actions and functional loss.

criteria.title: Progressive enhancement
criteria.rationale: Core functionality and acceptable enhancement need task-based interpretation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Complete key tasks with scripts and styles separately unavailable; distinguish lost decoration from blocked core service.

criteria.title: Carbon-aware design
criteria.rationale: Carbon-triggered variants need controlled signals and measured effects with user choice preserved.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise high/low-carbon or load states, compare resource use, and verify explanations and restoration controls.

criteria.title: Alternative browsing
criteria.rationale: Useful non-visual and indirect interaction depends on task equivalence and accessibility.
criteria.reviewRoute: Test representative tasks with assistive technologies, reader modes and relevant alternative inputs; record functional gaps.

criteria.title: Sustainable JavaScript
criteria.rationale: Unnecessary calculations, DOM work and requests need task-scoped profiling.
criteria.reviewRoute: Profile interactions and idle states; compare required output with repeated computation, DOM changes and network activity.

criteria.title: Energy-relevant APIs
criteria.rationale: An API's presence does not prove that it reduces energy or improves efficiency.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare matched scenarios using relevant APIs, such as visibility-driven suspension, against resource use and functionality.

criteria.title: API requests
criteria.rationale: Request necessity and minimal payloads depend on the task and data contract; client and server traces provide supporting measurements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect client and server traces, payload fields and purposes; measure redundant calls and over-fetching in representative tasks.

criteria.title: Dependency management
criteria.rationale: Regular removal and maintenance require a dependency inventory and project history.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review manifests, usage, removal decisions and dated dependency reviews rather than treating loaded bundles as the complete inventory.

criteria.title: Dependency necessity
criteria.rationale: Necessity, security assurance and maintained inventories require project decisions and records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare package/module costs and alternatives with security constraints, usage, inventory and review evidence.

criteria.title: Dependency updates
criteria.rationale: Current versions are detectable, but regular maintenance needs complete inventory and review history.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare lockfiles and deployed versions with supported releases, then inspect update cadence and justified exceptions.

criteria.title: Expected files
criteria.rationale: Named standard-file presence, response and basic syntax can be checked deterministically.
criteria.reviewRoute: Request the expected files at their defined locations, validate responses and record applicability or missing standard support.

criteria.title: Beneficial files
criteria.rationale: Discovery and syntax of named standard files are repeatable public checks.
criteria.reviewRoute: Fetch applicable beneficial files, validate recognized formats and distinguish presence from truth of any declarations.

criteria.title: Appropriate Implementation
criteria.rationale: Balancing implementation effort, runtime impact and user value is an architectural judgment supported by measured costs.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare implementation options using build/runtime measurements, maintenance effort, dependencies and user value.

criteria.title: Optimized methodology
criteria.rationale: Choosing native, existing or custom solutions requires interpreting performance, maintenance and security tradeoffs.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review native, existing and custom options against measured performance, tooling cost, support and trusted security components.

criteria.title: Static over dynamic
criteria.rationale: Static versus dynamic delivery can be compared quantitatively against declared update and functionality requirements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect rendering architecture, update needs and server measurements; compare a feasible static or cached alternative.

criteria.title: Extensions and plugins
criteria.rationale: Regular compatibility, efficiency and accessibility review requires plugin inventory and maintenance history.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect installed extensions and themes, review records and representative regressions or performance comparisons.

criteria.title: Interface components
criteria.rationale: Component overhead can be measured, while avoidable complexity requires a functionally equivalent comparison.
criteria.reviewRoute: Profile component bundles, rendering and interactions; compare simpler alternatives that preserve required behavior.

criteria.title: Versioning
criteria.rationale: Declared language and framework versions can be compared mechanically with stable releases.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect authoritative runtime/build version declarations and compare them with upstream releases; verify deployed identity separately.

criteria.title: Language choice
criteria.rationale: Language suitability depends on team capability, adoption costs and task-specific requirements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review language alternatives, workload measurements, maintenance ecosystem, costs and effects on team well-being.

criteria.title: Efficient database querying
criteria.rationale: Query plans and workload traces support repeatable comparisons of retrieval, filtering and database work.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect query traces and plans for key workloads; compare filtering, field selection and query counts at the database layer.

criteria.title: Reuse of retrieved data
criteria.rationale: Repeated retrieval is measurable within a declared request or process; source and traces expose the relevant work.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace representative requests or jobs and identify repeated retrieval of the same data before validating reuse changes.

criteria.title: Data minimization in queries
criteria.rationale: Returned fields and rows can be compared with declared data needs using source and workload traces.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare query projections and returned rows with application use; verify reduced retrieval preserves required output.

criteria.title: Data lifecycle controls
criteria.rationale: Retention, de-identification and purpose limitation require data governance and execution records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect data purposes, TTL policies, identifiers and deletion evidence across the relevant backend stores.

criteria.title: Provider selection
criteria.rationale: Transparent provider claims alone do not establish sustainability-led selection decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare provider disclosures and metrics with procurement criteria, service scope and selection rationale.

criteria.title: Efficient operation
criteria.rationale: Infrastructure efficiency over time requires operational monitoring and actions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review utilization, energy/water indicators and capacity changes across representative periods and workloads.

criteria.title: Equipment longevity
criteria.rationale: Hardware life extension and procurement practices require asset and maintenance evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect hardware age, utilization, patching, repairs and supplier longevity commitments.

criteria.title: Low-carbon electricity
criteria.rationale: Hosting electricity claims need location, supply and operational boundaries beyond a green label.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review grid/location data, on-site generation and backup supply with hosting decisions and reporting methodology.

criteria.title: Remaining emissions
criteria.rationale: Valid market-based claims depend on certificates, retirement and time/location matching.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect electricity volumes and certificates, matching rules, retirement evidence and double-counting controls.

criteria.title: Domain names
criteria.rationale: Registrar disclosures can be public, but their use in registration decisions needs project evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Check registrar/registry impact information and review how missing or available evidence informed domain choices.

criteria.title: Client-side caching
criteria.rationale: Correct reuse requires initial, repeat, update and authorization-state experiments.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare cold/warm requests, changed content and logout states; check reuse without stale content or unauthorized access.

criteria.title: Server-side caching
criteria.rationale: Cache benefits and correctness can be compared through controlled workload, update and authorization tests with server evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect caching layers and processing evidence, then test updates and authorization transitions for correctness.

criteria.title: Offline access
criteria.rationale: Meaningful essential functionality must be defined before offline behavior can be tested.
criteria.reviewRoute: Complete agreed essential tasks after network loss, including recovery and stale-data handling.

criteria.title: Server-side compression
criteria.rationale: Compression savings and processing tradeoffs require comparison rather than a header-only check.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare compressed and uncompressed representative file types for transfer, loading and processing, avoiding already-compressed assets.

criteria.title: Media compression
criteria.rationale: Useful compression requires size comparisons while preserving acceptable media quality.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect representative asset formats and compression opportunities; compare variants for quality, transfer and compatibility.

criteria.title: Error pages
criteria.rationale: Helpful recovery and safe disclosure require interpretation of error states.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trigger representative errors, assess explanations and recovery paths, and inspect exposure of sensitive or internal details.

criteria.title: Redirection
criteria.rationale: Chains and loops are measurable, but necessity, safety and proportionality need review.
criteria.reviewRoute: Crawl and exercise relevant links, validate destinations, measure chains and review intentional redirects against user and maintenance value.

criteria.title: Unused environments
criteria.rationale: Utilization and workload measurements can identify redundant capacity once required isolation and security constraints are defined.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect environment inventory, workload/utilization records and security constraints before proposing shutdown or consolidation.

criteria.title: Task automation
criteria.rationale: Appropriate automation and avoidable complexity need workflow interpretation, with run costs and source supporting the judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review CI/CD definitions and run histories; compare duplicated work, maintenance effort and platform impact.

criteria.title: Necessary tasks
criteria.rationale: Task necessity and ongoing review depend on the purpose and execution history of automation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect triggers, frequency and run results, then trace each job to a required outcome and remove proven duplication.

criteria.title: Automated scaling
criteria.rationale: Capacity optimization depends on infrastructure utilization, workload priorities and operating constraints.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review demand and allocation histories, autoscaling policies and controlled load tests for overprovisioning and contention.

criteria.title: Suspicious activity management
criteria.rationale: Effective bot restrictions need activity logs and decisions about legitimate access.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect crawler policies, control outcomes and logs; test representative authorized access without assuming all automation is harmful.

criteria.title: Refresh frequency
criteria.rationale: Refresh schedules can be compared quantitatively against declared freshness needs and resource costs.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare freshness requirements, refresh schedules and observed polling/cache behavior with measured resource use.

criteria.title: Data backups
criteria.rationale: Defined backup, restore, retention and access tests can assess security and incremental behavior using authorized operational evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review backup scope, storage/access settings, retention and restore tests, including user-identifiable data handling.

criteria.title: Carbon shifting
criteria.rationale: Controlled scheduling and placement comparisons can measure carbon-aware behavior within explicit residency, performance and security constraints.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare job timing/location and grid signals with measured energy, latency, security and data-residency requirements.

criteria.title: Protocol efficiency
criteria.rationale: Protocol support is detectable, but selecting efficient secure options requires scoped comparisons.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory negotiated protocols and legacy fallbacks; compare transfer performance against compatibility and security requirements.

criteria.title: Event-driven architecture
criteria.rationale: Equivalent server workloads allow quantitative comparison of event-driven and synchronous architectures.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare event-driven and synchronous designs with workload traces, processing, power, performance and operational complexity.

criteria.title: Data processing efficiency
criteria.rationale: Equivalent workloads and output requirements allow measured comparisons of processing placement and redundant work.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace processing stages and compare feasible placements under equivalent output, workload and security conditions.

criteria.title: Efficient location
criteria.rationale: Application data flows and traces support comparisons of processing placement and serialization overhead.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect data flows and measure transformation or serialization overhead near and far from the source.

criteria.title: Global CDNs
criteria.rationale: CDN benefit can be compared for a declared audience and workload using delivery and provider-impact measurements.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare delivery measurements by audience region with hosting/CDN footprints, caching behavior and local-hosting alternatives.

criteria.title: Sustainability commitment
criteria.rationale: Credibility of published CDN commitments can be assessed from attributed evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare scoped provider targets, methods, verification and progress; separate commitments from demonstrated reductions.

criteria.title: Inappropriate resources
criteria.rationale: Dynamic-resource suitability requires measured caching behavior and update characteristics.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare CDN hits, freshness, CORS and authorization behavior for changing resources; inspect configuration where public traces are insufficient.

criteria.title: Lowest requirements
criteria.rationale: Capacity can be compared with demand once service, recovery, security and resilience requirements are explicit.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare allocation with workload peaks, recovery/security obligations and tested headroom rather than average utilization alone.

criteria.title: Remove unused data
criteria.rationale: Obsolete-data removal requires inventory, usage and retention evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect data-age/access records, justified retention and completed deletion or archiving actions.

criteria.title: Lifecycle management
criteria.rationale: Storage tiers and lifecycle rules require operational policy and configuration evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review data classification, TTL/archive rules and access frequency against storage placement and executed transitions.

criteria.title: Efficient storage
criteria.rationale: Lasting value and safe removal depend on operational, analytical and legal purposes.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare stored datasets, duplicates and compression with use, regeneration cost and retention requirements.

criteria.title: Optimized logging
criteria.rationale: Logging scope, backups, privacy and scheduling depend on operational records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review log purpose, volume, retention, access, rotation and processing schedules; trace monitoring to useful corrective action.

criteria.title: Asset downloads
criteria.rationale: Useful downloadable alternatives depend on the asset and repeat-use task.
criteria.reviewRoute: Identify large durable assets, test download and offline reuse, and assess whether the alternative reduces repeated retrieval.

criteria.title: Public documents
criteria.rationale: Published policy clarity, accessibility and versioning can be assessed from public documents.
criteria.reviewRoute: Discover the relevant policy set, inspect language and accessible formats, and compare versions and declared scope.

criteria.title: Achievements and compliance
criteria.rationale: The criterion asks for useful public disclosure, which can be reviewed directly.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect the dedicated sustainability section for relevant achievements, evidence, updates and clear scope.

criteria.title: Governance over time
criteria.rationale: Implementation and monitoring over time require operational records, not a policy alone.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace goals through dated decisions, measurements, accountability and corrective actions across review periods.

criteria.title: Technology legislation
criteria.rationale: Legal compliance, advocacy and going beyond minimum obligations need organizational and specialist evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review applicable obligations, compliance evidence, advocacy and data-minimization decisions with qualified input where needed.

criteria.title: Advocate for sustainability
criteria.rationale: A named advocate does not establish expertise, authority, time or resources.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect the assigned role, responsibilities, digital expertise, allocation and evidence of active work.

criteria.title: Inform and aware
criteria.rationale: Making materials available does not prove delivery to all relevant participants.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review onboarding and workshops, intended audiences, delivery records and coverage gaps.

criteria.title: Routine training
criteria.rationale: Regular active skills development requires participation and recurrence evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect training schedules, attendance, refreshed content and how learning supports project sustainability work.

criteria.title: Active participation
criteria.rationale: Encouragement and organizational support require evidence of actual opportunities and resources.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review participation channels, shared initiatives, provided resources and examples of supported action.

criteria.title: Training materials
criteria.rationale: Suitable training content is reviewable, but delivery and maintenance require records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect materials against current policies, version history and evidence of delivery to relevant audiences.

criteria.title: Incentivize progress
criteria.rationale: Time allocation and incentives require evidence of organizational practice.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review recognition, allocated learning time, benefits and progress tracking without assuming an announcement proves delivery.

criteria.title: Communication of impact
criteria.rationale: Useful, understandable environmental feedback and meaningful choices require content judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise relevant decisions, inspect impact explanations and verify the assumptions behind displayed comparisons.

criteria.title: Life-cycle assessment
criteria.rationale: A complete LCA needs a defined functional unit and lifecycle inventory.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect boundaries, inventory, methods, factors, exclusions and evidence supporting lifecycle impact claims.

criteria.title: Competitor impact
criteria.rationale: Comparability and justified additional impact depend on service value and aligned assessment boundaries.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare alternatives using equivalent functional units, lifecycle scopes and user value, recording data gaps.

criteria.title: Tooling impact
criteria.rationale: Pipeline-wide tooling impact needs development and third-party usage evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inventory build, development and external tools; assess measured or estimated lifecycle impacts with declared boundaries.

criteria.title: Web sustainability goals
criteria.rationale: Published goals, measurable indicators and reported progress can be reviewed directly.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect targets, baselines, timeframes and progress reports for specificity and consistency of measurement.

criteria.title: Obtaining verification
criteria.rationale: Independent assurance requires scope, independence and verification evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect assurance statements, verifier independence, methods, exclusions and the claims actually verified.

criteria.title: Maintaining verification
criteria.rationale: Reassessment and claim updates require a dated assurance and evidence history.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare successive verifications and new evidence with the claims currently published.

criteria.title: Policies and practices
criteria.rationale: The criterion asks for published disclosure policies aligned with recognized standards.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review public reporting commitments, applicable standards, coverage and clarity of disclosed procedures.

criteria.title: Impact reports
criteria.rationale: Annual publication and comparisons can be assessed through publicly available report series.
criteria.reviewRoute: Locate annual reports, check reporting periods and compare progress claims with prior reports and goals.

criteria.title: Disclosure reporting
criteria.rationale: Transparent reporting practices require evidence of how figures are produced and maintained.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect reporting controls, data sources, boundaries, review responsibilities and publication history.

criteria.title: Impact reduction
criteria.rationale: Reduction claims need quantitative reconciliation and qualitative checks for misleading boundaries.
criteria.reviewRoute: Recalculate disclosed reductions, compare baselines and scopes, and investigate exclusions, double counting and selective presentation.

criteria.title: Theory of change
criteria.rationale: Revenue-impact relationships and iterative improvement need business-model evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review revenue streams, impact pathways, measurement methods and decisions demonstrating improvement over time.

criteria.title: Management and maintenance
criteria.rationale: The required management approach can be assessed as a maintained document.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect product maintenance documentation for clear responsibilities, lifecycle scope and revision history.

criteria.title: Planning strategy
criteria.rationale: Plans must be implemented and maintained across products and services.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review maintenance/security plans, resourcing and records showing sustainability priorities used in delivery.

criteria.title: Resourcing products
criteria.rationale: Staffing, budgets and sustained maintenance cannot be inferred from a working site.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect resourcing commitments, technical-debt work and continuity of support across the product lifecycle.

criteria.title: Resource measurement
criteria.rationale: Maintenance-integrated measurement and decision incentives need longitudinal project evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review resource metrics, baseline changes and maintenance decisions; assess whether incentives encourage useful outcomes.

criteria.title: Failure indicators
criteria.rationale: Documented risk indicators also need active monitoring and corrective action.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect KFI definitions, thresholds, monitoring records and examples of risks influencing decisions.

criteria.title: Continuous improvement
criteria.rationale: Embedded improvement requires evidence connecting decisions to sustainability outcomes.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace changes to environmental and operational measurements, explanations and review decisions.

criteria.title: Retrospectives conducted
criteria.rationale: Regular research, debt reduction and learning require team process evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect retrospectives, allocation of time and resulting research, maintenance or delivery changes.

criteria.title: Iterative consideration
criteria.rationale: A sustained improvement record and necessary analytics require history and project objectives.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review iteration decisions, analytics purposes and resource/performance consequences against user needs and stated goals.

criteria.title: Functionality decisions
criteria.rationale: Lifecycle decisions about features need usage, impact and maintenance evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace representative retain/change/remove decisions to user value, resource impact, usage and ownership records.

criteria.title: Feature changes
criteria.rationale: Clear structured change communication can be reviewed from releases and documentation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare release notes or change logs with sampled feature changes for consistency, versioning and practical consequences.

criteria.title: Sustainable Development Goals
criteria.rationale: Published SDG alignment needs a reasoned comparison with the service and specific targets.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect the sustainability statement and assess whether named goals and targets have a plausible, scoped relationship to the service.

criteria.title: Creation evaluation
criteria.rationale: Desirability, feasibility and viability decisions require research and business context.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review alternatives, user demand, delivery constraints and the decision to create or retain the service.

criteria.title: Obstacle consideration
criteria.rationale: Barriers and justified safeguards require task-based accessibility and fairness judgment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise representative access paths under user constraints and distinguish unnecessary barriers from necessary protections.

criteria.title: Vetting potential partners
criteria.rationale: Sustainability-led procurement requires criteria, due diligence and applied decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review supplier selection and management records, lifecycle considerations and responses to identified risks.

criteria.title: Collaborative measurement
criteria.rationale: Collaborative impact tracking requires supplier participation and shared evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect agreed indicators, responsibilities, measurements and actions involving affected parties.

criteria.title: Informative partner promotion
criteria.rationale: Public partnership disclosure and its claimed collective impact are directly reviewable.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect partnership descriptions, scope and supporting impact information; separate promotion from demonstrated outcomes.

criteria.title: Living wage
criteria.rationale: This criterion requires a public commitment, not proof of payroll compliance.
criteria.reviewRoute: Check the public commitment's scope across employees, contractors and other affected parties; record any exclusions.

criteria.title: Incentivization
criteria.rationale: Embedded incentives need policy and evidence of their application.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review incentive criteria, affected parties and implemented arrangements against the stated impact goals.

criteria.title: Employee benefits
criteria.rationale: Actual benefits and their relation to resources require employment and organizational evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect benefit eligibility, provision and resourcing; distinguish published promises from delivered benefits.

criteria.title: Decision-making
criteria.rationale: Meaningful participation, authority and human appeals require governance and process evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review decision rights and participation records; exercise public automated-decision controls and inspect human-review procedures.

criteria.title: DEJI practices
criteria.rationale: Published commitments and explanations can be judged for scope and relevance.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect DEJI commitments and explanations of how they address exclusion and sustained access; distinguish explanation from verified outcomes.

criteria.title: DEJI training
criteria.rationale: Providing training requires evidence of relevant content and actual delivery.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review DEJI training coverage, audiences, participation and treatment of digital exclusion and algorithmic harms.

criteria.title: DEJI improvements
criteria.rationale: Published progress requires comparable measurements across hiring, leadership and operations.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect indicators, denominators, periods and progress claims; request underlying records where aggregates are insufficient.

criteria.title: Data practices
criteria.rationale: Public policy review cannot establish the required data protection and governance practices.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare accessible policy documents with data flows, controls, applicable standards and evidence of stronger protections where needed.

criteria.title: Data ownership
criteria.rationale: Visible data controls do not prove retention and deletion across stores, backups and caches.
criteria.reviewRoute: Exercise access/export/opt-out flows, then trace purpose, retention and deletion through relevant systems and records.

criteria.title: Outdated content
criteria.rationale: An archive or schedule does not establish executed expiration and deletion across content and data.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect published schedules, automated rules and completed review/archive/deletion examples; test lightweight archive discovery.

criteria.title: AI and data collection
criteria.rationale: Dataset necessity, sourcing, validation and fairness require model/data governance evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect dataset inventories, provenance, screening, minimization, evaluation and retention for the stated task.

criteria.title: Business adaptation
criteria.rationale: Support for employees affected by technological change requires workplace evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review consultation, training, transition resources and records of how affected staff were supported.

criteria.title: Environmental responsibilities
criteria.rationale: Technology necessity and lifecycle impact require model, infrastructure and business context.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review alternatives, deployment/optimization measurements and first/third-party lifecycle accounting with stated uncertainty.

criteria.title: Automated tooling
criteria.rationale: A controlled test can assert bot identity and opt-out behavior; access to the operated tool is separate from test determinism.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect crawler/tool identities and configuration, then test opt-out handling and user-agent declarations in controlled scenarios.

criteria.title: Quantum resilience
criteria.rationale: Cryptographic migration depends on data lifetime, sensitivity and dependency assessment.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review cryptographic inventories, threat/lifetime assumptions and migration planning against applicable NIST guidance.

criteria.title: Fuel divestment
criteria.rationale: Actual divestment and financial relationships require financial evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect banking, sponsorship and investment policies plus records demonstrating movement away from fossil-fuel exposure.

criteria.title: Responsible finance
criteria.rationale: Budgeting and financing for long-term responsibility require financial and maintenance context.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review funding horizons, maintenance allocations and environmental criteria in financial decisions.

criteria.title: Philanthropy policy
criteria.rationale: A giving policy alone does not establish aligned philanthropic partnerships.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect the policy, partner selection and evidence of active partnerships supporting stated objectives.

criteria.title: Voluntary work
criteria.rationale: Support for voluntary work needs evidence of time, resources or completed activity.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review supported programs, allocation and participation records and benefits to the intended organizations.

criteria.title: End-of-life care
criteria.rationale: The criterion asks for clear documented end-of-life guidance that can be inspected directly.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review disposal, archive and deletion instructions for scope, responsibilities and practical usability; do not infer that retirement occurred.

criteria.title: E-waste management
criteria.rationale: Responsible hardware treatment requires asset disposition and service-provider evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Trace retired assets through reuse, repair, redeployment or certified disposal and inspect provider policies.

criteria.title: E-waste policy
criteria.rationale: Repair and recycling commitments can be assessed from maintained policy documents.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect repair/recycling policy scope, responsibilities and support for repair; distinguish policy adequacy from execution.

criteria.title: Refurbishment strategy
criteria.rationale: Prioritizing existing hardware requires evidence of procurement and redeployment decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Compare equipment requests with repair/refurbishment options and completed reuse or purchase decisions.

criteria.title: Right to repair
criteria.rationale: Repairability, parts pricing and user capability require product and supply evidence beyond web copy.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect repair instructions, parts availability/prices and restrictions; seek practical repair evidence for the product scope.

criteria.title: Environmental budget
criteria.rationale: Lifecycle budget criteria must be actively applied and communicated.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect lifecycle limits, affected audiences and decisions or alerts showing those limits influenced delivery.

criteria.title: Performance budget
criteria.rationale: A measured small page or budget file does not establish active enforcement and reduction.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect thresholds and CI/monitoring results, then trace exceedances and measured changes to actions.

criteria.title: Human budget
criteria.rationale: Sustainable engineering budgets require staffing, workload and worker well-being evidence.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review effort metrics, planning, workload limits and employee feedback rather than inferring sustainability from delivery speed.

criteria.title: Measurable improvements
criteria.rationale: Baseline comparisons and improvement claims can follow an explicit quantitative reconciliation.
criteria.reviewRoute: Check equivalent scopes and methods, recalculate claimed changes and inspect evidence for attribution and uncertainty.

criteria.title: Open source governance
criteria.rationale: Sustainable selection, approval and release practices require governance and applied decisions.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review open-source policies, approvals, releases and maintenance responsibilities for reuse and long-term support.

criteria.title: Collaboration and contribution
criteria.rationale: Regular community contributions require evidence across time and forms of support.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review code, time and financial contributions, their cadence and their connection to shared maintenance or reuse.

criteria.title: Plan of action
criteria.rationale: Maintained and tested incident response requires exercise and incident records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Review plans, tests, residual risks and actual incidents, then trace lessons to operational or retirement decisions.

criteria.title: Audience awareness
criteria.rationale: Clear incident and risk communication can be assessed from public status and notification records.
criteria.reviewRoute: Inspect representative incident communications for affected services, availability/data risks, updates and practical user guidance.
